cards.title: Accops HyID (Silver/Gold/Platinum) vs Cisco Duo Editions (Free, MFA, Access, Beyond): Feature Checklist Spreadsheet (2021)
cards.key_problem: A prospect pricing Cisco Duo per edition needs to see which Duo tier a given HyID edition matches, and where Duo needs an extra gateway or cloud sync that HyID does on-premise.
key_outcomes: One-sheet x/no checklist: four Duo editions with their list prices of the time (Free up to 10 users, MFA, Access, Beyond - USD 3/6/9 per user per month) against HyID Silver, Gold and Platinum

Sections: user trust (push, security keys/U2F, OTP, SMS, hardware tokens, self-enrolment), device trust (device dashboard, health, BYOD vs corporate), adaptive policies (network, location, user group, Tor blocking, anomalous access, MDM/endpoint-management gating), secure app access and SSO
HyID-only rows: connector for third-party fingerprint/face authentication and Accops' own fingerprint/face authentication
Where Duo Network Gateway gives internal web/SSH/cloud app access, HyID needs an additional HySecure gateway (Silver/Gold) or has HySecure included (Platinum)
HyID rows for RADIUS/LDAP proxy, local database/LDAP without Active Directory, and on-premise deployment with no user sync to a third-party cloud
Some mobile device-trust rows are marked 'MDM needed' on the HyID side
cards.brief: A small single-sheet Excel checklist (created March 2021, last saved March 2023) comparing Cisco Duo's four editions with HyID's three editions row by row. Cells are 'x' or 'no' (a few 'MDM needed', 'Custom checks' or 'Additional HySecure Gateway'). There is no narrative, scoring or pricing for HyID. In the extracted text empty cells collapse, so read the column position in the original sheet before quoting a specific row.
cards.use_for: A Duo displacement or head-to-head MFA deal: 'which HyID edition matches Duo Access/Beyond?', 'does HyID need a gateway for internal apps?', 'can HyID run fully on-premise without cloud user sync?'. Internal checklist to build a customer-facing table from, not a document to send.
cards.stale_risk: Created March 2021, last saved March 2023 (the '2021-01-01' prefix is the bulk-rename date). Duo's editions and prices have since changed (Duo now sells Essentials/Advantage/Premier), so the Duo columns are out of date. HyID edition contents may also have changed.

cards.title: Event Request Template and Event SOP (Internal Marketing Form): Proposal Fields, Success Metrics, CEO Approval, Partner-Event Responsibilities and KPIs
cards.key_problem: Sales and partner managers proposing an event need a standard way to request it, get it approved and agree who owns what, so marketing can plan and audit it.
key_outcomes: Request sheet rules: the proposer must get the CEO's approval first; the request's ageing starts only once it reaches marketing with that approval; brand audit is marketing's job, post-event tracking the proposer's

Request fields: event type, proposer, city, mode, date, focus verticals, objective, two short-term and two long-term success metrics, budget, success owner, CEO approval, and for partner events the partner name, category, minimum promised audience, partner FY target and last-FY revenue

Drop-down lists: event types (with / through / to partner, existing customers, sponsored, Accops-own, partner connect, partner acquisition), approval states, Indian cities plus UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and North Africa, objectives (reconnect, reinforce, empower, new customer acquisition, thought leadership, brand visibility)

Metric options: attendees, decision-makers attended, 5/5 feedback ratings, booth visitors, net new opportunities, opportunity conversion %, partner orders in the FY, net new conversion, upsell, cross-sell

SOP tab (images): per-event-type planning and execution tables, e.g. 'With Partner Events': budget approval by the executive leadership team, date and venue by partner + partner manager, venue and collateral by the partner to Accops brand guidelines, partner must deliver the minimum committed audience, speaker is the regional business head or presales head, leadership attends only for high-value partners, post-event follow-up by the partner manager measured in MQLs, auditing by marketing
cards.brief: An internal Excel workbook (created August 2022, last saved September 2025) with an 'Event Request' form sheet, an 'SOP' sheet whose content is pasted slide images (an 'Event Request CHECKLIST' and per-event-type responsibility/KPI tables) and a lookup sheet feeding the drop-downs. cards.title: Japan Partner Sales Bootcamp 2026 - 4-Hour Deck in English (Confidential, 20 Aug 2026): VDI-First Order, 'What's New' Release History (HyWorks 3.6-4.1, HySecure, HyID), New VDI Cases (HFT Firm, Telecom, Pharma, UK TPA), Spectra UEM, IRIS Architecture and 2027 Roadmap
cards.client: Named case slides: an Indian high-frequency trading firm (Linux developer VDI, SEBI compliance), a large Indian telecom (VMware Horizon replacement with ARS 3.0), a global pharma company (Citrix/VMware consolidation, SAP on GCP), the largest TPA in the UK (Citrix replacement for about 5,000 users), Japan's leading university (HyLabs), India's largest private bank (biometric MFA), a shipbuilder (Airbridge), the Government of India ZTNA order
cards.client_actual: Graviton Research Capital, Airtel, Dr. Reddy's, Diligenta, Kyoto University (called 'Japan's second-largest university'), L&T Shipbuilding, NIC; working notes on slide 129 mention IKEA, Sul America, Airtel, LIC MF, BFL and Bharat Forge
regulations: APPI (Japan Act on the Protection of Personal Information)
cards.key_problem: Japanese partners need the 2026 bootcamp re-ordered around VDI (Accops' strongest line in Japan), with what has changed in each product and where the roadmap is going.
key_outcomes: Structure: same AI-exploit opening and company section as the India master, then VDI first (slides 30-83), ZTNA (84-118), identity (119-136) and other products (137-152)

Japan tailoring: business drivers cite the Japan data protection law and rising laptop/workstation costs; GPU workstations '2x-4x' price escalation; a third-party thin-client support slide (NComputing LeafOS, Mintwave, 'upcoming Dell, HP') sourced from Japanese catalogues

'What's new' slides: HyWorks feature evolution 3.6 to 4.1 HF2 (OpenStack, Proxmox, Nutanix API v4, OpenShift, Morpheus, APIs), HyLabs evolution, Workspace client, Teams offload, Photon, new ARS, a list of HySecure enhancements (continuous re-evaluation, geolocation login restriction, DC-DR sync, software asset collection)

New VDI case slides not in the India edition: HFT firm (Linux developer VDI + ZTNA + MFA with Forcepoint DLP), telecom (VMware Horizon replacement, Azure Traffic Manager, ARS 3.0), pharma (SAP on GCP as published app, Turbo Layer 3), UK TPA (Citrix replacement after licence cost rose up to 4x)

Other: 'India chooses sovereignty' NIC ZTNA slide, HyDesk, NanoOS, Spectra UEM & DEX (GA 31 Dec 2026) with eight management areas, Huddle, Proxmox, IRIS (V1.0 15 Dec 2026; architecture with IRIS SaaS India and Japan; 'launch plan with VDI: 2026 Q2'), 'Roadmap for 2027' (IRIS GA, IRIS Japan, LTSR, migration path)
The CEO personal-identifiers slide is not in this edition; the 2030 roadmap with the ARR target and the Gartner market-sizing slide are

It re-orders the India master around VDI and adds release-history ('What's new') slides, four new named VDI case studies, Spectra and an IRIS architecture and 2027 roadmap.
